data.name: Sir! I'd Like To Report A Bug!
data.detailed_description:
After some new prototype tech goes screwy and causes bugs to escape into the world only one man can save the day.

That man is Reggie! An average, couch potato games tester with no talents what so ever! Help our new savior venture to and from work while the world around him slowly glitches out and breaks during his working week.

Overcome obstacles such as killer cars, lava floors and one seriously @!&#^% off sun, tackle the horrors of the daily commute but with more fire and randomness. Don't think that this is a fun, cute adventure though, the world wants you dead! Dead! Dead! DEAD!

Still think you're up to the challenge and can help save the day?

Features:

  • Classic hard-as-nails 2D platformer gameplay
  • Seriously, this game is hard. It will make you rage.
  • Very shiny pixel art, look at how beautiful it is!
  • A raving, chip-tune inspired soundtrack. Turn that volume up!
  • Each level is unique thanks to the army of bugs blowing up the world!
  • Jam packed with humor and references
  • Challenge mode for those that fancy a little bit more
  • The only game in history to ever feature flying old people, bouncing buildings and a level based on Eiffel 65's "Blue (Da Ba Dee)"
  • Is it really too hard for you? Fine! Have a brand new easy mode with checkpoints
  • More responsive control thanks to keyboard and controller support
  • In game achievements
  • Trading cards to collect or flog for a few pennies!

reviews.review:
Sir! I’d Like To Report A Bug! is a retro-style action platformer developed and published by Lord Puggington Games that transforms software errors, corrupted programming, and complete digital instability into the core of its gameplay experience. Instead of avoiding glitches and broken mechanics, the game fully embraces them, building an unpredictable and chaotic adventure where players must survive inside a malfunctioning world constantly collapsing under the weight of its own corrupted code. Combining classic side-scrolling platforming with absurd humor, difficult level design, and intentionally unstable environments, the game delivers a strange but memorable experience that feels both nostalgic and creatively unhinged.

The story centers around Reggie, an ordinary game tester whose boring daily routine is destroyed when experimental software begins malfunctioning in catastrophic ways. Digital bugs escape containment and infect reality itself, turning the world into a chaotic nightmare filled with impossible hazards and unpredictable environmental disasters. Reggie suddenly finds himself trapped in the middle of a crisis far beyond his abilities, becoming humanity’s accidental hero despite having no real qualifications for the task. The premise is intentionally ridiculous, and the game leans heavily into that absurdity from beginning to end, creating a humorous atmosphere that constantly mocks gaming culture, programming failures, and classic platformer tropes.

Gameplay revolves around traditional side-scrolling platforming, but the unstable nature of the world constantly changes the rules. Levels behave unpredictably as environments glitch, distort, and break apart in real time. Floors may suddenly become deadly, objects can behave incorrectly without warning, and entire sections of stages seem to malfunction as the player progresses. Rather than simply memorizing enemy patterns and jumping between platforms, players must adapt to constantly shifting conditions where the world itself becomes the greatest obstacle. This unpredictable structure helps separate the game from more conventional retro platformers because every level feels intentionally unstable.

One of the strongest aspects of the game is its creativity. Nearly every stage introduces some bizarre new concept or environmental hazard tied to the idea of broken programming. Players may find themselves avoiding collapsing roads, surviving deadly weather, dodging absurdly dangerous traffic, or navigating sections where ordinary physics no longer function properly. The constant introduction of strange mechanics and ridiculous hazards keeps the gameplay fresh and prevents the experience from feeling repetitive despite its relatively straightforward core mechanics.

The platforming itself is deliberately difficult in the spirit of old-school arcade games. Precision jumps, careful timing, and repeated trial-and-error are central parts of the experience. The game expects players to memorize hazards, learn environmental patterns, and improve gradually through repeated attempts. Deaths are frequent, especially during later levels where environmental chaos becomes increasingly intense. For fans of retro platformers, this difficulty creates a rewarding sense of accomplishment whenever difficult sections are finally completed. However, players unfamiliar with classic arcade-style design may find the experience frustrating at times due to its unforgiving nature.

Fortunately, the game eventually introduced a more accessible difficulty mode that adds checkpoints and reduces some of the harsher punishment systems. This allows newer players to enjoy the humor and creativity without being completely overwhelmed by the challenge. Even with these adjustments, the game still demands patience and concentration because the unstable environments constantly create new dangers that require fast reactions and careful movement.

Visually, Sir! I’d Like To Report A Bug! uses colorful pixel art combined with glitch effects and exaggerated environmental distortion to create the illusion of a game falling apart in real time. The retro-inspired presentation works extremely well with the concept because the world genuinely feels corrupted and unstable. Objects flicker unexpectedly, environments break visually, and animations occasionally appear intentionally damaged in ways that reinforce the game’s chaotic identity. Despite the intentionally broken appearance, the art style remains expressive and energetic throughout the adventure.

The soundtrack supports the action with fast-paced retro-inspired music that captures the intensity of classic arcade games. Chiptune-style tracks help maintain momentum during difficult platforming sequences while distorted sound effects reinforce the game’s malfunctioning digital atmosphere. The music rarely slows down, constantly pushing players forward even during repeated failures and frustrating moments.

Humor plays a major role in making the experience enjoyable despite its high difficulty. The game constantly uses absurd situations, visual jokes, and exaggerated hazards to keep the tone entertaining rather than oppressive. Many levels feel intentionally ridiculous, turning ordinary situations into life-threatening disasters simply because the game world itself is broken. This comedic approach helps reduce frustration because even repeated failures often become amusing due to the sheer insanity of what is happening on screen.

The game also offers extra challenge modes and additional objectives for players seeking even more difficulty after completing the main campaign. Achievements, hidden surprises, and optional challenges provide additional replay value beyond simply reaching the ending. Although the campaign itself is relatively short, the unpredictable level design and high difficulty encourage multiple attempts and repeated playthroughs.

However, the game’s intentionally chaotic presentation can occasionally create problems. Some visual effects and environmental distortions make hazards difficult to read during faster sections, leading to moments where deaths feel unfair rather than deserved. Certain platforming mechanics can also feel slightly imprecise under pressure, especially during sequences requiring perfect timing. Additionally, while the short length prevents the gameplay from becoming repetitive, it also means some of the game’s most creative ideas disappear before they are fully explored.

Despite these shortcomings, Sir! I’d Like To Report A Bug! succeeds because of its originality and complete commitment to its strange concept. It transforms software instability into an entertaining gameplay mechanic while delivering the kind of brutal challenge associated with classic platformers. The combination of glitch-inspired level design, retro visuals, absurd humor, and unpredictable environmental hazards creates a memorable experience that feels genuinely unique among indie platformers.

For players who enjoy difficult retro games, experimental platformers, and self-aware gaming humor, Sir! I’d Like To Report A Bug! offers a chaotic and highly creative adventure filled with digital madness and relentless surprises. Its unstable world, challenging gameplay, and bizarre sense of humor create an experience that proudly embraces being broken in the most entertaining ways possible.

Rating: 6/10
